title: Frozen stress/state/tangent history, and the Residual Assembler's inputs (v1)
x-what-this-is: The ingredients one verified corpus case produced, frozen so the Residual Assembler can be driven from what the pipeline actually emits rather than from a reference model written to make the assembler pass. It holds numbers the pipeline computed and the identity of the file they came from, never the file.
x-three-state-rule: Every field typed [boolean, null] has three answers and null is never a pass. A fixture frozen before a check existed does not carry that check's key; refusing it would treat 'frozen before the check' as 'failed the check', and passing it silently would treat it as 'passed'. So claims_checked and claims_not_carried name which is which.

source_id.description: Identity is the path within the corpus cache, never a basename.

transform_fingerprint.description: REQUIRED. The transform this fixture's numbers were produced by. A consumer must refuse a fixture whose fingerprint does not match the store it is read beside: the numbers are evidence about a transform that has since changed.

material.description: Provenance is REQUIRED here, not optional. A fixture is what later runs are compared against forever after; a constant in one with no provenance is indistinguishable from an invented one.

material_point.description: The tensor convention the arrays below are written in. Stated rather than assumed: engineering shear read as tensorial is wrong by two in three components and right everywhere else.

finite_history.description: Whether the run behind this fixture was finite END TO END, not only over the carried window. Six increments out of hundreds are finite in a run that went to NaN at increment 200, so scanning only what is carried cannot tell a verification from the salvageable prefix of a failed analysis.

increments_carried.description: Distinct (step, increment, time) among those rows. This is what 'how long is this history' means.

records_carried.description: Rows in the carried history. NOT the number of increments.

material_points_per_increment.description: Rows per increment, or 0 when uneven. Uneven is not a number to average.

material_point_carried.description: Which integration point these rows are, so a reader is not left assuming the element had only one.

material_points_available.description: How many points the RUN wrote, which is not how many are kept.

then.description: one point per increment means one row per increment; anything else is two counts confused

history.description: The stress / state / tangent history at one material point: what the Residual Assembler consumes. 'original' is the author's build; 'converted' is the transformed build. Both are carried because the difference between them is the evidence, and a fixture holding only one of them cannot be differenced.

ddsdde.description: The material tangent, row-major, ntens*ntens long. In the list because a fixture whose stress is finite and whose tangent is not would freeze a NaN that only shows up once somebody assembles a stiffness.

element.description: Which element. Half of the material-point identity.

point.description: Which integration point. A C3D8 writes one row per point per increment, so without this rows cannot be grouped.

step.description: Which step. REQUIRED, and half the identity of an increment: Abaqus restarts increment numbering in every step, so (increment, time) alone cannot say which *BOUNDARY block was in force.

items.description: JSON has no NaN or Infinity literal, so a non-finite value can only arrive as a string or a null; both are refused by this type. A NaN frozen into a fixture does not fail, it propagates, and the comparison that should have caught it is being made against the NaN.

x-identity-rule: FIVE fields name one row: element, point, step, increment, time. Abaqus numbers increments from 1 again in every step, so a four-step J2 cycle has four increment 1s -- measured on the committed j2_props fixture, where they carry stresses of 269.2, 1571.5, -264.0 and -182.6, four different states of the material. A consumer reconstructing boundary conditions from 'increment' alone picked the wrong one and was wrong by 3.0 relative: a different deformation, not a tolerance. element and point are the other half -- a C3D8 writes one row per integration point, so without them rows cannot be grouped into increments at all.
x-count-rule: RECORDS and INCREMENTS are two counts and neither may stand for the other. A record is one material point of one increment, so a 35-increment C3D8 history is 280 records. An exporter reported records as increments, a loader compared one against the other, and a complete history was refused as '35 of the 280 asked for'. records_carried = increments_carried x material_points_per_increment whenever the points per increment are even; 0 there means uneven, which is not a number to average because an increment short of a point did not produce the state a comparison would compare.
